objective: Sequential focused-task campaign to improve validated learning efficiency and higher-order quantitative-research capability.
research_conclusion: The short-horizon momentum edge (lookback 3/5/10, 1-day hold, daily rebalance) is COST_ROBUST under the repository's existing cost model: realistic and 3x-conservative costs leave candidate per-fold medians essentially unchanged (decay ~0.000-0.001 for 9/10 assets) and the predeclared edge count stays >=6/10 at every lookback. Qualification: the existing engine's slippage is directionally symmetric (a credit on sells) and cancels over round trips, so the tested cost channel is commissions (~0.11%/yr AMZN drag); robustness to true directional slippage/market impact is UNVERIFIED. Process improvement indicated: add a mandatory cost-model audit to the standard gate stack, because the frictionless prior evidence and this model both omit true slippage.
unverified: Robustness to TRUE directional slippage / market impact is UNVERIFIED: the existing engine adds slippage to the fill price on both buys and sells, so slippage is a credit on the closing side and cancels over round trips; the cost test therefore stresses commissions only.

The lookback 3/5/10 grid is near-degenerate: candidate medians are identical across lookbacks for every asset because sign(mean log return over the window) = sign(closes[i]/closes[i-lookback]-1); the grid does not independently stress lookback, so cost results transfer across lookbacks.
